parole.testo: Terminology of the religious sphere borrowed from Hebrew אָדָם (āḏā́m, “man, person”), with a foreign pattern like عَالَم (ʕālam, “world”).

According to Arthur Jeffery it appears first in discussions of dietary laws and thus is likely borrowed from Hebrew בְּהֵמָה (bəhēmā́). Else it belongs to the root ب ه م (b h m) to which there is also بَهْمَة (bahma, “lamb”). Compare Ugaritic 𐎁𐎅𐎎𐎚 (bhmt) and Ge'ez ብህመ (bəhmä, “to be dumb, to be spee

parole.significato: a scholar (especially one that is highly regarded and respected by a certain group and is deemed to be an authority)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew חָבֵר (ḥɔḇer, “comrade”) in a specific meaning as used for sectarian cadres. Merged with Etymology 3 by analogy with the use of ink by religious clerks and scribes, hence "a man of learning", hence "a scholarly theologian", hence "an authority in matters of religion".
From plural of Biblical Hebrew שרף.
